panels.rationale: Single-image figure: grayscale ultrasound of a neonate (article title: 'Proximal Ureteral Atresia in a Caribbean Neonate With Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney') showing a large cystic lesion in the region of the right kidney marked by a black arrow and the on-image text 'CYSTIC LESION' (10.17 cm). The disease-focused article title plus the panel-specific captioned manifestation (cystic lesion of the right kidney with multiple septations, left kidney structurally normal) supports attribution to multicystic dysplastic kidney. The appearance is a large septated cystic mass rather than the textbook cluster of multiple non-communicating cysts, hence 'variant' and moderate confidence; no skin is visible so skin tone is null and ethnicity is not explicitly stated in the caption or in-text mentions.

in_text_mentions: rance. A nasogastric (NG) tube was inserted, and the patient was kept nil by mouth (NPO). Antibiotics were commenced, and abdominal X-rays and an ultrasound scan (USS) were ordered. The USS showed a cystic lesion with multiple septations seen on the right side of the abdomen, extending to the right hemidiaphragm (Figure 1). It displaced the small and large bowel to the left of the midline and the inferior vena cava (IVC) and aorta posteriorly. It measured 10.2 cm x 8.5 cm x 5.4 cm. The left kidney was visualized and appeared structurally normal, along with the other intra-abdominal structures.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Prenatal MRI panel shows fetal left renal cystic lesions in a patient with MCDK, supporting MCDK-related non-communicating renal cysts. b: Axial CT panel shows unilateral left renal cystic replacement, a classic imaging manifestation of multicystic dysplastic kidney. c: Follow-up MRI shows an atrophic left kidney with multiple cysts, consistent with an involuting/atrophic variant of multicystic dysplastic kidney.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (a, b, c, d, e, f). a: Histology from the renal specimen of an infant with multicystic dysplastic kidney, showing dysplastic/atrophic parenchymal architecture. b: Histology of the MCDK kidney with marked dysplastic/atrophic changes, abnormal vessels and parenchymal destruction. c: PAS-stained renal histology showing immature glomeruli and interstitial fibrosis, characteristic of MCDK dysplasia. d: Renal histology from MCDK showing fibromuscular proliferation around the calyx, part of the dysplastic kidney pathology. e: Renin immunohistochemistry of the MCDK kidney, showing renin in immature glomeruli/tubules; disease attribution from the MCDK case report and dysplastic renal context. f: Additional renin immunohistochemistry of the MCDK kidney, showing renin in immature glomeruli/tubules; attributed to the MCDK case report.
panels.attribution_text: Sugimoto et al. Pathophysiological clinical features of an infant with hypertension secondary to multicystic dysplastic kidney: a case report.. BMC nephrology 2021. doi:10.1186/s12882-021-02249-6. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: a Light microscopy of the entire cross-section reveals abrupt transition from normal to atrophic cortex with lobar atrophy (Masson-trichrome staining, 4×). b Tubular atrophy, marked abnormal blood vessels with wall thickening (short arrow), gathered glomeruli, and parenchymal destruction are observed (Masson-trichrome staining, 20×). c Diffuse immature glomerulus with interstitial fibrosis is observed (Periodic acid-Schiff staining, 250×). d Fibromuscular tissue proliferation is observed around the renal calyx (Masson-trichrome staining, 40×). e, f Renin localized partially in the proximal tubules and the parietal epithelium of the Bowman’s capsule in the immature glomeruli (short arrow) (Renin antibody staining, 200×)

in_text_mentions: The patient had normal renal function tests for his age. On examination, hypospadias was confirmed as seen in Figure 1. In utero ultrasonography showing bilateral MCDK is shown in Figure 2. Soon after delivery, another ultrasound was done, which is seen in Figure 3. The patient was followed on a monthly basis, and after 6 weeks, repeat renal function tests were done, which were unremarkable. Figure 4 shows an ultrasound scan after 6 weeks post‐delivery.
